title: The sea (Exodus 14:10–31)
hookLine: the sea ahead, chariots behind: stand still and see

cards: They're barely out of Egypt when Pharaoh changes his mind. Why did we let our slaves go? He takes six hundred chosen chariots and all the chariots of Egypt and gives chase.
The Israelites are camped by the sea. They look up and see the dust cloud coming. Water in front, army behind, no way around.

And the people turn on Moses, in the King James translation: "Because there were no graves in Egypt, hast thou taken us away to die in the wilderness?" Leave us alone, they say. Slavery was better than this.

teach.b: Moses answers: "Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the LORD, which he will shew to you to day." And: "The LORD shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace."
Then God says almost the opposite: "Wherefore criest thou unto me? speak unto the children of Israel, that they go forward." Stand still, and go forward. Both.
The stillness isn't doing nothing. It's stopping the panic, so you can see the way when it opens. Moses stretches out his hand.

teach.h: A WALL ON THE RIGHT AND LEFT.
teach.b: A strong east wind blows all night and drives the sea back, and the people walk through on dry ground, "and the waters were a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left."
The Egyptians follow, the wheels come off their chariots, the water returns, and the army is lost. The Hebrew name for this water is yam suph.

teach.h: YAM SUPH: RED SEA, OR REEDS?
teach.b: Older translations say Red Sea, but suph is the word Exodus uses for the reeds where baby Moses's basket was hidden, so some readers say Sea of Reeds. The text never says where it was.
A later Jewish story tells of a man named Nahshon who walked into the water up to his neck before it parted.
Christians have read this crossing as a picture of baptism: Paul writes that the Israelites were all "baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea."
Exodus fourteen is read at the Easter Vigil in Catholic churches and others that keep that night, when new Christians may be baptized. Through the water, from slavery to freedom.

how: Exodus 14 is read at the Easter Vigil in Catholic churches and others that keep the Vigil, linking the crossing of the sea to baptism, and some Christians turn to "stand still, and see the salvation of the LORD" in times of fear.

games.why: "Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the LORD." then God says: tell them to go forward. stillness first, then the step.

practice: Stand up if you can, feet flat, arms loose, and think of the worry that feels like chariots behind you right now. Don't run from it or fight it; just stand still, let your breathing slow, and notice that you are here, standing.
If you pray, you can say Moses's words, fear not, stand still; if you don't, just stay still and see what you notice.
